questions.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=y\,i-x\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
questions.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i-x\,j \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot (-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+(-5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-25{sin}^{2}⁡t-25{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(-25)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-25t\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =-25(2\pi )-0 \\  & =-50\pi \end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=2x\,i+2y\,j$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}=9$ oriented counterclockwise.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of our curve as

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1.
$$

The closed curve $C$ is the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $3$ and $1,$ respectively. It can be parameterized in the counterclockwise direction as

$$
r(t)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2x\,i+2y\,j \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot (-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }-16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8(\frac{-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t}{2})\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =-4(-1+1) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y)=({e}^{x+y}-4x)\,i+({e}^{x+y}+6y)\,j.$ Which of the following statements are true?

- $F$ is **not** conservative
- ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$ for any piecewise smooth path $C\in {R}^{2}$
- ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r\ne 0$ for some closed paths $C\in {R}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
If $F$ is a conservative vector field on ${R}^{2},$ then the circulation $Γ=0$ for any *closed* path $C\in {R}^{2},$ that is 

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.
$$

We notice that $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field with domain $D={R}^{2}.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\frac{∂Q}{∂x}={e}^{x+y}.
$$

With that in mind, let's consider each statement in turn:

- Statement I is false. The vector field $F$ is conservative since the partial derivatives are equal and continuous everywhere on ${R}^{2}.$

- Statement II is false. The result $Γ=0$ applies to closed curves only.

- Statement III is false. The circulation $Γ=0$ for any closed path $C\in {R}^{2}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "None of the statements are true."

choices.value: None of the statements are true

answer_fields.correct_value: None of the statements are true

- $F$ is conservative
- ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$ for any ellipse $C\in {R}^{2}$
- ${∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0$ for any closed path $C\in {R}^{2}$

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r=0.
$$

We notice that $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field with domain $D={R}^{2}.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have
